options: A browser-only feature with no installation required
A desktop client that talks to Salesforce via SOAP or Bulk API
A Salesforce report type for exporting dashboards
A Chrome extension for editing records inline
questions.explain: Data Loader is a client application you install on your machine, which communicates with Salesforce through its SOAP or Bulk APIs.

questions.q: What must be installed before Data Loader itself?
options: A Salesforce Enterprise Edition license
Java Runtime Environment (JRE) 17 or later
Microsoft Excel
The Salesforce CLI
questions.explain: Data Loader no longer bundles its own Java runtime, so JRE 17+ has to be installed first.

questions.q: Which operation is greyed out until a separate permission is granted?
options: Export
Insert
Hard Delete
Upsert
questions.explain: Hard Delete permanently removes records without sending them to the Recycle Bin, so it requires the Bulk API Hard Delete permission before it's available.

questions.q: What's the key difference between Export and Export All?
options: Export All also returns soft-deleted and archived records
Export works only on custom objects
Export All requires Bulk API; Export does not
There is no difference — they are aliases for the same operation
questions.explain: Export All retrieves everything Export does, plus soft-deleted and archived records that Export alone leaves out.

questions.q: Why would an admin choose Data Loader over the Import Wizard for a given job?
options: Data Loader is required for any job touching Leads
The job needs an unsupported object, complex mappings, or scale beyond 50,000 records
The Import Wizard has been deprecated by Salesforce
Data Loader doesn't require logging in, unlike the wizard
questions.explain: Data Loader earns its extra setup cost when the job needs an object the wizard doesn't support, complex field mappings, or volume past the wizard's 50,000-record cap.
